Keeping the triple lock on pensions will cost an extra £20bn a year by 2050, according to a leading think tank. As calls grow for the guarantee to be scrapped, the Institute for Fiscal Studies said the Government's pledge to increase state pension payments by at least 2.5% a year was already costing taxpayers £16bn more every year compared to a simple earnings link. –

Major indices were in the red at the close of trading on Wednesday, with markets still grappling with another jump in oil prices and the inflation worries that come with it.
At the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was 0.77% lower at 52,380.66, while the S&P 500 shed 0.48% to 7,636.36 and the Nadsaq Composite saw out the session 0.64% weaker at 26,253.34.
